So, we come to the end of the course and all roads lead to Jerusalem. So, we're going to take everything we've learned so far and combine it into a narrative about today and the future. The grand thesis of this class is that six societies control the world, and this something you can never prove. But let me propose a theory of how we can approach truth. If you have a theory or an idea or a narrative and it does these three things, then it approaches the truth: first, it connects the past; second, it explains the present; third, it predicts the future.

Does this narrative help us put past events into a coherent story that we can understand? Does it help us better understand the world we live in? And most importantly, does it allow us to make certain predictions about how events should develop? If these predictions turn out as expected, then our theory of truth is more likely correct.

Just because things turn out the way we predict doesn't necessarily mean that our theories are 100% correct. Correlation does not necessarily mean causation. So, with very little evidence, I'm going to present a theory about how the world works, a story about how we got to where we are. This is speculation, and some may call it a conspiracy theory. Take what I say with a grain of salt, ask good questions, and doubt what I say. But this theory, even though it doesn't make much sense and you may not believe it, does help us connect the past, explain the present, and predict the future.

So, without further ado, let's go into this theory. You remember Jacob Frank who founded the Sabatine Frankus movement. He will convert to the Catholic religion and encourage his followers to do the same while infiltrating secret societies. One of his patrons is Mayor Rothschild, founder of the Rothschild banking dynasty. He introduced Jacob Frank to another person named Adam Weiss Hot in Bavaria.

In present-day Germany, Adam Weishot is a former Jesuit and a member of the Catholic Church, also a Jew. Let's assume they knew each other. Together, they will create a new organization called the Illuminati, which controls the world. There is a legend that Adam Weishot encouraged his followers to infiltrate another organization called the Freemasons. These were prominent members of European society—intellectuals like Gerta, nobility, and bankers.

The Illuminati has an alliance of Jesuits, Jews, Frankists (Sepian Frankas), Catholics, and Freemasons. There is a legend that Adam Weishot was eventually arrested for conspiracy by authorities, disbanding the organization. However, others argue that he spread this legend to generate publicity. In reality, the Illuminati did not disband and still exists today.

Why would they do this? Secret societies depend on publicity for recruitment. Free publicity from reading about a secret organization trying to conquer the world, which authorities don't like, is valuable.
